record.what_it_does: Copper is a CRM built around Google Workspace that helps sales teams manage leads, contacts, companies, opportunities, projects, and tasks.
record.auth_notes: API keys are generated by an individual user in Copper's web app under System settings > API Keys and sent as X-PW-AccessToken/X-PW-Application/X-PW-UserEmail headers. OAuth2.0 is the vendor-preferred method for partner/third-party integrations, but registering an OAuth app requires emailing partners@copper.com to receive a client_id and client_secret before the Authorization Code flow can be used.
record.access_notes: There is no permanent free plan — copper.com/pricing offers only a free, no-credit-card trial ('Start free, no credit card required') leading into paid Basic/Professional/Business per-seat plans; API key generation appears available to any account (not gated to a specific paid tier in the plan comparison doc), but sustained use requires converting to a paid subscription. OAuth2 additionally requires manual app registration via partners@copper.com, which is an extra approval step layered on top of the trial/paid account requirement.
record.main_blocker: OAuth2 app registration requires manually emailing partners@copper.com for client_id/client_secret

evidence.quote: There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0.
You have registered your application (partners@copper.com) and received your client_id and client_secret credentials
Start free, no credit card required.
To generate an API token, in the Copper web app go to System settings > API Keys and click the 'GENERATE API KEY' button.
The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.
The CData Python MCP Server extends this capability to hundreds of data sources by leveraging CData Python Connectors.
Webhooks allow systems integrated with Copper to receive near real-time notification of certain events

record.open_questions: Could not confirm from a vendor page whether API key generation is restricted on the lowest (Starter/trial) tier specifically; the plan-comparison help article does not list 'API access' as a gated feature, suggesting it's available on all tiers, but this is inferred by absence rather than an explicit statement. Also note a same-named but unrelated company, Copper.co (crypto custody, developer.copper.co), surfaced in search results and must not be confused with Copper CRM (copper.com) — it was excluded from this research.
